interpretation.diagram_classification: cosmological / meteorological diagram: wind rose (wheel of the twelve winds) with the four cardinal directions
interpretation.interpretation: The diagram is a wind wheel. A circle is divided by twelve radial bands into twelve sectors. Each sector carries the name of a wind, often with a second (Greek or Latin) name or a short explanatory phrase. The four cardinal points are written outside the ring: ORIENS (top, east), MERIDIES (right, south), OCCIDENS (bottom, west) and SEPTENTRIO (left, north). The wheel is therefore oriented with east at the top. The sector names are consistent with this: the winds of the east and south-east ("eurus", "euro notus", "sub solanus", "apeliotes"), the south ("auster", "notus"), the south-west and west ("africus", "libs", "zephyrus", "fabonius"), and the north-west and north ("chorus", "circius", "septentrio", "aquilo", "boreas"). The words "vulturnus" and "calcias" probably belong to the upper-left sector. The central empty circle is the hub of the wheel. The alternation of green and tan spokes probably marks the cardinal axes (the green horizontal and diagonal spokes) against the intermediate directions, but this is not certain. Phrases such as "haec sunt", "appellantur" or "distincte", "a parcias" and "signa" suggest explanatory prose. They probably say that these winds are called by these names and distinguished by their regions. The diagram thus works as a schematic compendium of wind names arranged around the horizon, in the tradition of medieval texts on natural science and computus.
interpretation.evidence: Wind names are legible in the sectors (e.g. "auster", "africus", "aquilo", "boreas", "circius", "euro notus", "zepphir", "fabonius", "uulturnus", "sub solanus"). The cardinal terms ORIENS, MERIDIES, OCCIDENS and SEPTENTRIO are written outside the ring. The wheel form with twelve radial divisions and a central hub is visible. Several Step 1 transcriptions are uncertain, particularly in the lower, upside-down sectors, where text was recorded with low certainty. Some sector names in Step 1 are also partial or merged (e.g. "uento auster africus uibonom", "ordine chorus agrestis"). The Step 1 predicates for the cardinal labels SEPTENTRIO and MERIDIES ("above" the ring) are only approximate, because these words sit beside the ring, not above it. The "XII" in the right-hand sector supports the count of twelve winds. The specific source is not named because it cannot be identified with confidence.
